paragraphs.en: The concept of collective intelligence has fascinated researchers and {politicians} alike.It suggests that large groups of people can make remarkably {logical} decisions when their judgments are {averaged} out.
paragraphs.cn: 集体智慧这一概念令研究人员和 <u> 政治家 </u> 们着迷。这个概念表明，如果将大量人群的判断 <u> 平均化 </u> ，他们能够做出极为 <u> 合乎逻辑 </u> <u> 的 </u> 决策。

paragraphs.en: On {March} 7, 1907, the English {statistician} Francis Galton published a paper which illustrated what has come to be known as the ”wisdom of crowds” effect.The estimation experiment he {conducted} showed that in some cases, the average of a large number of independent estimates could be quite accurate.This proves that collective intelligence is far more than just a {fancy} theory.
paragraphs.cn: 1907年 <u> 3月 </u> 7日，英国 <u> 统计学家 </u> 弗朗西斯·高尔顿发表了一篇论文，阐述了所谓的”群体智慧”效应。他 <u> 实施 </u> 的估算实验表明，在某些情况下，大量独立估算结果的平均值可能是相当准确的。这证明”集体智慧”不止是一个 <u> 花哨的 </u> 理论。

paragraphs.en: This effect {capitalizes} on the fact that when people make errors, those errors aren't always the same.There's a {distribution} of knowledge and perspectives.Some people will tend to {overestimate} , and some to {underestimate} .When enough of these errors are averaged together, they {cancel} each other out, resulting in a more accurate estimate.In more {technical} {terms} , the wisdom of crowds requires that people's estimates be independent, meaning that the sample must include both mighty {lions} and humble {sheep} .If for whatever reasons, people's errors become {correlated} or {dependent} , the {accuracy} of the estimate will decline.
paragraphs.cn: 这种效应 <u> 利用 </u> 了这样一个事实：当人们犯错时，这些错误并不总是相同的。知识和观点存在着一种 <u> 分布 </u> 。有些人倾向于 <u> 高估 </u> ，而有些人则倾向于 <u> 低估 </u> 。当足够多的错误被平均起来，它们就会相互 <u> 抵消 </u> ，从而得出更准确的估算。用更 <u> 专业的术语 </u> 来说，群体智慧要求人们的估算是相互独立的，这就意味着，样本中必须既有”强大的 <u> 狮子 </u> ”，又有”谦逊的 <u> 绵羊 </u> ”。如果出于某种原因，人们的错误变得相互 <u> 关联 </u> 或相互 <u> 依赖 </u> ，那么估算的 <u> 准确性 </u> 就会降低。

paragraphs.en: But a new study led by Joaquin Navajas offered an interesting twist ( (转折) ) on this {classic} {phenomenon} .The key finding of the study was that when crowds were further divided into smaller groups that were allowed to have a discussion, the averages from these groups became even more accurate.For instance, the average {obtained} from the estimates of four discussion groups of five members was significantly more accurate than that from 20 independent individuals.
paragraphs.cn: 但是，华金·纳瓦哈斯牵头的一项新研究为这个 <u> 经典现象 </u> 带来了有趣的转折。这项研究的主要发现是，当人群被进一步划分为更小的小组，允许组员间进行讨论时，这些小组得出的平均值甚至变得更加准确。例如，从由五个成员组成的四个讨论小组的估算中 <u> 得出 </u> 的平均值，明显比从二十个独立个体的估算中得出的平均值要准确得多。

paragraphs.en: In a {follow-up} study with 100 university students, the researchers tried to get a better sense of what the group {members} actually did in their discussion.Did they tend to go with those most {confident} about their estimates? Did they follow what the {majority} said? This happened some of the time, but it wasn't the {dominant} response.Most frequently, the groups reported that they ”shared arguments and {reasoned} together.” {Somehow} , these arguments and {reasoning} resulted in a global reduction in error.The research's {implications} for group discussion and {decision-making} are {enormous} .
paragraphs.cn: 在一项针对100名大学生的 <u> 后续 </u> 研究中，研究人员试图更好地了解小组 <u> 成员 </u> 在讨论中实际做了些什么。他们会倾向于听从对自己的估算最 <u> 有信心的 </u> 人吗？他们会听从 <u> 大多数人 </u> 的意见吗？这种情况虽然时有发生，但并非 <u> 最主要的 </u> 反应类型。最常见的情况是，这些小组报告称，他们”共同讨论论据，并一起进行 <u> 推理 </u> ”。 <u> 不知何故 </u> ，这些论证和 <u> 推理 </u> 使得误差在整体上有所减少。这项研究对小组讨论和 <u> 决策 </u> 活动具有 <u> 巨大的潜在影响 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: Modern {institutions} tend to utilize this phenomenon to {predict} market trends or {vote} on consumer preferences.However, the wisdom of crowds isn't {permanent} .It might fail when faced with complex challenges such as {election} outcomes.We must remain {honest} about both the potential and limitations of crowd wisdom after all.
paragraphs.cn: 现代 <u> 机构 </u> 往往利用群体智慧现象来 <u> 预测 </u> 市场趋势，或对消费者的偏好进行 <u> 表决 </u> 。然而，群体智慧并非 <u> 永远 </u> 存在。在面对 <u> 选举 </u> 结果等复杂数据时，群体智慧可能会失效。毕竟，我们必须 <u> 坦然 </u> 面对群体智慧的潜力和局限性。 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
